messages:
morgan: seeing a sharp spike in 5xxs from apac-southeast2 starting ~10:40 UTC, GPU pool reports 60% degraded nodes. P50 latency up 120ms. Can we soft-evac and route some traffic elsewhere?

ria: on it — checking pool health and node errors now. any recent deploys to that pool?

alex: no deploys in last 2hrs. infra metrics show kernel OOM events on a subset of nodes, container restarts ~2-3/min. autoscaler hasn't added new nodes for that pool (look like image-pull backoff on init?).

samir: if autoscaler blocked we should avoid hard cutover. propose gradual weight shift from apac->eu by 10% increments every 5m, TTL 30s so clients re-resolve quickly. keep a canary at 5%.

charlie: +1. Also enable model-variant fallback for latency-sensitive routes (quantized variant) to reduce GPU pressure during shift. Put a flag in routing-policy to prefer quantized variant in target regions.

morgan: running quick runbook snippet: ``gslbctl override set --from apac-southeast2 --to eu-west --weight 0.1 --ttl 30 --reason "partial gpu pool degrade"`` will apply a soft divert. want me to apply or have oncall run it?

infra-oncall: I'm around, I can run. Before we change weights: threshold for rollback? set rollback if apac error rate goes above +2% or eu latency P95 > 700ms or backend rate limit errors > 5/min.

ria: confirmed kernel OOMs correlated with a bad kernel patch on recent node image. We can hot-fix node image but takes ~30-45min to reprovision safely. Recommend soft divert now.

samir: go ahead infra-oncall, apply 10% -> eu-west, monitors on. I'll set alerts for errors and model-fallback ratio.

gslb-bot: Applied override: from=apac-southeast2 to=eu-west weight=0.10 ttl=30 actor=infra-oncall id=ovr-20240404-01

morgan: traffic shift started. early telemetry: apac 5xxs down 15%, eu request rate +8%, eu P95 +40ms (within margin).

charlie: toggled routing preference: prefer model=redwood-quant-4q in eu for affected routes. This should reduce GPU memory pressure.

alex: note: cost team FYI — cross-region egress between apac->eu will spike. We should track cost delta; if we sustain >20% extra egress, consider CPU fallback or local latency tradeoffs.

ria: can we give a quick command I can run to ramp to 25% over 3 steps?

samir: use: ``gslbctl override bump --id ovr-20240404-01 --step 0.1 --every 300s --max 0.25`` — that will increment 10% every 5m until 25%. I'll keep watch on alerts.

infra-oncall: kicking the bump. running now.

gslb-bot: Scheduled bump: id=ovr-20240404-01 next_in=300s step=0.10 target=0.25

morgan: 5m update: apac 5xxs continue trending down, eu P95 stable. total cross-region egress +14% vs baseline. still under cost threshold.

ria: node reprovision in apac started (hotfix image). ETA ~32min.

charlie: quick checklist reminder in case of surge during ramp: 1) pause bump 2) enable local cache TTL=60 3) route heavy-offload to dedicated burst pool if available 4) consider temporary request-rate cap per tenant.

alex: billing alert set with cost-team for +25% egress. notify if hit.

samir: bump complete, current override weight=0.25. continuing to monitor for 20m then decide whether to drain more or let reprovision finish.

morgan: reprovision finished — apac nodes healthy now, OOMs gone. Recommend gradual roll-back of override: step -0.1 every 5m until back to 0.

infra-oncall: rolling back using ``gslbctl override bump --id ovr-20240404-01 --step -0.10 --every 300s --min 0``

gslb-bot: Scheduled bump: id=ovr-20240404-01 next_in=300s step=-0.10 target=0.00

ria: metrics post-rollback: apac request rate recovering, 5xxs at baseline, eu request rate decaying to normal. no further action needed.

alex: cost impact overall small; egress blip peaked at +18% and dropped. good runbook behavior.

morgan: nice work team. we'll document this in the incident playbook (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/INC-APAC-GPU-2024) and add a note to autoscaler to handle image-pull backoffs faster.

samir: +1. Closing thread in ~1h unless anyone wants follow-ups. :thumbsup:

infra-oncall: ack :white_check_mark:
